events.text:
## Recommendation
- **Go to Grand Haven.** I'd expect boat fishing there to be about **2 of 4 (average)**. Run 60-120 ft of water, with lines and spoons around 35-100 ft down.
- **St. Joseph is the upside pick.** I'd rate it about **2 of 4**, with a wide range (1 to 4). Run 80-90 ft of water with spoons.
- **Ratings for the week:** Grand Haven 2, St. Joseph 2 (wide range), South Haven 2, Muskegon 2. The reports don't separate these ports much. Grand Haven is the pick because its report is the newest.
- **Lures to start with:** green and orange spoons, white flasher flies, and meat rigs. These were the most-cited lures across the recent boat reports.

## Why
- Grand Haven has the newest report (July 24), so it's the best guide to this week. That report described boats catching Chinook and coho 35-100 ft down in 60-120 ft of water, though the quality was not rated or only below average (Grand Haven, 2024-07-24).
- St. Joseph's July 10 report was excellent (4), but it is 20 days old, and the July 3 St. Joseph report was only below average (1). I'd expect that spread to make it a riskier pick than its best report suggests.
- Past seasons at similar surface temperatures (about 70 F) mostly rated boat fishing average (2), with a range of 0 to 3 (historical reports, Grand Haven, Muskegon, South Haven, St. Joseph, 2022-2023). That is why I'm putting every port at 2.

## Evidence
**Recent reports (salmon, boat)**
- Grand Haven, 2024-07-24: Chinook were caught 35-100 ft down in 60-120 ft of water. Green and orange spoons and white flasher flies worked. Chinook quality was not rated; coho was rated 1 (below average). A few salmon were also caught on meat rigs and glow plugs, rated 1.
- Grand Haven, 2024-07-10: quality 2 (average). Best action was 40-100 ft down in 65-120 ft of water. Meat rigs "worked very well," along with orange spoons and white flasher flies.
- Muskegon, 2024-07-10: quality 2. Salmon were caught 40-100 ft down in 70-120 ft of water. Meat rigs and flasher flies were productive.
- South Haven, 2024-07-10: quality 2. Mixed coho and Chinook; best depths were 75-80 ft and 105-110 ft of water. Rotators and flies worked. On 2024-07-03 it was rated 3 (good) at 90-110 ft.
- St. Joseph, 2024-07-10: quality 4 (excellent). Chinook and coho were caught in 80-90 ft of water, mostly on spoons. On 2024-07-03 only a few coho were caught at about 100 ft, rated 1.
- Muskegon, 2024-07-03: salmon were caught 30-90 ft down in 70-130 ft of water. Orange spoons and white flasher/fly combinations worked; not rated.

**Past seasons (history, not current)**
- At similar surface temperatures (about 70 F), boat reports in past Augusts and late Julys were mostly 1-3. For example, Muskegon on 2023-08-02 was 3 (good), and Grand Haven on 2022-07-14 was 0 (slow).
- Past reports suggest late-July and August boat bites often happen in 50-150 ft of water and that a sharp water drop can bring fish in. I'd expect the same pattern this year, but I can't confirm it.

**Conditions now**
- The tool returned a summary for the week before July 30, not live data. Surface water was about 73 F at St. Joseph, 71 F at South Haven, and 68 F at Grand Haven and Muskegon (buoy readings, measured).
- The NOAA cold-layer model and wind forecast were not available, so I can't say where the 52-58 F water sits this week.

## Caveats
- The newest report is 6 days old (Grand Haven). The St. Joseph, South Haven, and Muskegon reports are 20 days old, so those ratings are mostly based on older conditions.
- The ratings are my estimates from these reports, not DNR forecasts. Please check the latest DNR bulletin and the current forecast before you go.
- Surface water is 68-73 F, which is above the 52-58 F range Chinook prefer (general guidance, NY DEC). Fish are likely holding deeper, so trolling at depth matters more than the surface reading.
- Wind is unknown from these results. If the forecast is strong (sustained 20+ mph or high waves), skip the boat trip and try a pier.
